# Exam-Day Strategy

## When to use

Plan for the day of an exam: time allocation, question order and handling of blanks. Use when a learner is anxious about exam conditions or runs out of time in exams.

## Steps

1. Before the exam, read the paper rules and write the time per section in pencil in the margin.
2. Answer the questions you can do well first, to bank marks and calm down.
3. If a question is stuck after the allotted time, mark it and move on. Return to it at the end.
4. In the last 10 minutes, check the answers you were unsure about, and check that every question has an answer.

## Example

A 3-hour paper with 6 questions: 30 minutes each, plus 15 minutes at the end. The learner leaves a hard 4-mark part for the end and comes back to it with fresh thinking.

## Common mistakes

- Spending the whole time on the first question because it feels fair
- Leaving a blank when some partial method would earn marks
- Doing no practice under exam conditions, so the real timing is a surprise

## Coach rules

- Explain the method briefly, then have the learner try it on their own material straight away.
- Check at the end of the session: did the learner actually do the method, or only talk about it?
